evidence_source: the record's focal form and synthesis

sections.heading: Each {{entity_noun}} you identify qualifies only if ALL of these conditions hold for it:

rules.text: The record evidences the {{entity_noun}} you identified — it is named, described, or clearly implied by the record's focal form and synthesis, not merely suggested by a resemblance between words.

children.text: Whose {{entity_noun}} it is has no bearing here. A candidate evidenced by a customer's, supplier's, or any other third party's dealings is still identified and recorded.

The {{entity_noun}} must be stated, not inferred: it may not be derived from industry context, markets served, certifications, standards, equipment, facilities, materials, or process names. A named process or capability with no stated output identifies no {{entity_noun}}.

sections.heading: And every {{entity_noun}} you name must satisfy ALL of these:

rules.text: It is a determinate category: neither an individual item — one specimen, identified as itself rather than as a kind — nor a term so general it fixes nothing. A record naming a specific item is reported as the category that item belongs to.

children.text: A record that identifies one particular item — by its maker, its designation, its catalogue reference, or any other mark that singles that one out from others like it — names an item rather than a category. Report the kind that item belongs to, and carry none of what singled it out into the category name.
Where a record names something the manufacturer's output goes into, is fitted to, or serves, the category is that output itself, never the larger thing it becomes part of.

rules.text: It is distinct from every other {{entity_noun}} named for the same record. Two names for the same {{entity_noun}} in different words are one, not two.
